concepts_addressed: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that businesses frequently fail in international expansion by copying their domestic (American) playbook directly into new country markets without adapting products to local cultural norms and consumer preferences. The error is presenting international expansion as merely launching in new geographies without localizing the actual product.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Consumer packaged goods businesses expanding internationally
Expansion from US market into markets with distinct cultural consumption norms (e.g., UK, Mexico, Canada)
bounded_by: May not apply to software or digital products where format is not culture-dependent

claims.text: Greg Short argues that successful international market entry requires partnering with local people in each target country to co-develop products that fit that country's culture, rather than assuming the home-market product will transfer unchanged.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.topic: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand
conditions: Physical consumer product businesses entering international markets
Markets with distinct local consumption norms
claims.mechanism: Local partners have knowledge of cultural preferences and consumption patterns that a headquarters team lacks, making product-market fit achievable only through local collaboration.

examples.text: Greg Short describes how his company tailors its energy drink can size for each country it launches in. In the US, the standard is a 12-ounce can. In the UK, consumers are accustomed to energy drinks in a smaller format (approximately 7 ounces / 250 milliliters). Rather than forcing the American 12-ounce format into the UK market, the company adapted the product size to match local expectations.

practices.text: When entering any international market, work with local people in that country to co-create a product that makes sense for the local culture rather than importing the home-market product unchanged.
practices.topic: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand
